questions.text: According to SPP 202, what percentage of total design fees is earned during the Bidding or Negotiation Phase?

rationale.b: 10% is not a standard individual phase fee for Bidding or CA.
rationale.d: 20% is not the standard for this phase; Design Development is 25%.
rationale.correct: The Bidding or Negotiation Phase earns 5% of the architect's total design fees, representing the phase where the cumulative total reaches 95% (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Bidding Assistance Phase earns 5% of total design fees.

questions.text: According to SPP 202, what does the architect furnish to bidders during the Bidding Assistance Phase?

options.text: Recommendations for which bid to accept, including a detailed analysis of each bid's compliance with project specifications
Complete sets of Bid Documents covering direct and indirect costs
Agreements to cover any bid shortfalls, ensuring that all financial gaps are addressed prior to contract award
Financing arrangements for selected contractors, including interest rate negotiations and payment schedules

rationale.a: Bid recommendations are made after bids are analyzed, not furnished with documents.
rationale.c: The architect does not provide financial guarantees.
rationale.d: The architect does not arrange contractor financing.
rationale.correct: For competitive bids, the architect furnishes complete sets of Bid Documents loaned to bidders covering direct and indirect costs (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Architects furnish complete Bid Documents to prospective bidders.

questions.text: What is the primary responsibility of the architect regarding bidder questions during the Bidding Assistance Phase?

options.text: Ignore bidder questions to maintain confidentiality
Provide guidance to specific bidders to favor particular contractors
Respond to bidder questions to clarify contract documents
Require all questions to be submitted only in writing without response

rationale.a: Questions deserve professional responses for accurate bidding.
rationale.b: Architects must treat all bidders equitably.
rationale.d: Architects provide clarification through various appropriate means.
rationale.correct: The architect assists in responding to bidder questions regarding contract documents (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Architects respond to bidder questions on contract documents.

questions.text: What percentage of total design fees is earned during the Construction Administration Phase according to SPP 202?

rationale.b: 10% is the combined total of Bidding and CA, but CA alone is the 5% balance.
rationale.d: 20% is not the standard for this phase.
rationale.correct: Construction Administration earns the remaining 5% balance of the architect's total design fees under SPP 202 (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Construction Administration Phase earns the final 5% balance of the total design fees.

questions.text: What is the cumulative fee percentage earned upon completion of the Bidding Assistance Phase according to SPP 202?

rationale.a: 85% is not a standard cumulative milestone in SPP 202.
rationale.b: 90% is the cumulative total through the Contract Documents phase.
rationale.d: 100% is reached only after the Construction Administration phase is completed.
rationale.correct: Cumulative through Bidding: SD (15%) + DD (25%) + CD (50%) + Bidding (5%) = 95% of total fees (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Bidding Assistance phase brings the cumulative fee to 95% of total design fees.

questions.text: Considering Bidding Assistance (5%) and Construction Administration (5%) phases together, what is the cumulative fee percentage for these two final phases?

rationale.a: 5% is the fee for either Bidding or CA individually.
rationale.c: 15% was the previous calculation based on an incorrect 10% CA fee.
rationale.d: 20% does not correspond to these two phases combined.
rationale.correct: Bidding Assistance (5%) + Construction Administration (5%) = 10% combined for the post-contract document stages (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Final two phases earn a 10% combined fee percentage.

questions.text: Why does Construction Administration earn only the remaining 5% balance of total fees despite potentially extending over months or years according to SPP 202?

options.text: Long timelines deserve high fees regardless of work scope, which is a common misconception among clients
By construction phase, major design work is complete; the role shifts from creator to administrator and inspector
Construction Administration requires minimal architect involvement, focusing primarily on oversight and coordination
The fee is arbitrary and should be negotiated for each project, reflecting the unique demands of each construction phase

rationale.a: Fees reflect work scope and creativity, not duration.
rationale.c: Construction Administration involves significant responsibility and oversight.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 reflects that by construction, the major design work is complete; the architect's role shifts from creator to administrator and inspector, justifying the final 5% balance allocation (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: CA fee reflects administrative role; 95% of design work is already billed.

questions.text: What is a key responsibility of the architect during Construction Administration regarding contractor and owner claims?

options.text: The architect automatically approves all claims without review, assuming all parties have acted in good faith and according to contract terms.
The architect makes decisions on all owner and contractor claims relating to execution and contract document interpretation
The architect ignores claims to avoid conflict, thereby maintaining neutrality and focusing on project completion.
The architect sides exclusively with either owner or contractor, depending on who has the stronger contractual position.

rationale.a: Claims require professional evaluation and decision-making.
rationale.d: Architects decide claims impartially based on contract documents.
rationale.correct: The architect makes decisions on all owner and contractor claims relating to execution and progress of work or interpretation of Contract Documents (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Architects adjudicate claims during construction administration.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as an activity during the Bidding Assistance Phase according to SPP 202?

options.text: Preparing bid documents and invitation to bidders
Assisting with establishing prospective contractor lists
Conducting construction work based on winning bids
Helping organize pre-bid conferences

rationale.a: Bid documents preparation is an explicit Bidding Assistance activity.
rationale.b: Assisting with contractor lists is an explicit Bidding Assistance activity.
rationale.correct: Construction work is performed by contractors, not the architect during Bidding Assistance. The architect prepares bid documents, assists with contractor lists, conducts conferences, and analyzes bids (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Architects prepare bidding, not perform construction work.

questions.text: According to SPP 202, when does Construction Administration begin?

options.text: During the Bidding Assistance phase, when the architect provides support in evaluating contractor bids and proposals
After the contractor is selected and commences work
During Design Development, as the architect begins to coordinate with consultants and contractors
Before Contract Documents are completed, allowing for early input on construction feasibility

rationale.a: CA begins after bidding is complete.
rationale.c: CA occurs after all design phases.
rationale.d: CA begins after Contract Documents approval.
rationale.correct: Construction Administration begins after the contractor commences work and continues until final project completion and turnover to the owner (SPP Doc 202).
rationale.takeaway: Construction Administration begins when construction work starts.
